- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply a 5–10% downward correction to forecast starting 2 days after sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, apply mean reversion: forecast = 0.8×prior + 0.2×true (for next 5 days).  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d), model tends to overestimate supply impact; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.
